identity_marker: rectangular wooden slate with distinct double horizontal lines, a 1-inch piece of white chalk, a tiny wet sponge cube, and a small dry cloth
continuity_anchors: resting on a flat wooden desk under bright, even overhead classroom lighting
video_goal: Demonstrate the Wet-Dry-Try method for teaching cursive handwriting using a Handwriting Without Tears wooden slate, sponge, and chalk.
single_prompt: From an over-the-shoulder view, two hands place a rectangular wooden slate with distinct double horizontal lines squarely onto a flat wooden desk under bright, even overhead classroom lighting. A hand sets down a 1-inch piece of white chalk, a tiny wet sponge cube, and a small dry cloth directly next to the wooden slate. The thumb and index finger pinch the small wet sponge cube, lifting it from the desk. The wet sponge presses onto the bottom line of the slate, glides up to the middle line, and curves back down, leaving a dark, wet trail in the shape of a cursive 'c'. The hand drops the sponge and picks up the small dry cloth, pinching it tightly. The dry cloth traces the exact path of the wet cursive 'c', erasing the moisture and leaving a dry, faint outline on the slate. The fingers pick up the small piece of white chalk, adjusting into a standard tripod grip. The chalk tip touches the bottom line of the slate and draws a smooth, upward curving stroke to the middle line. The chalk reverses direction, tracing back down the curve to the bottom line, and extends a small upward tail to complete the cursive 'c'. Without lifting the chalk, the hand sweeps the chalk tip up from the tail of the 'c' to form a cursive 'a', linking the two letters seamlessly. Finally, the hand lifts the chalk away, revealing the connected cursive letters 'ca' resting perfectly between the double lines of the wooden slate.
